summary: The balance comes from CONTA.SALDO; for individuals (PF) CONTA.BLOQUEADO is subtracted, for companies (PJ) it is not. Formatted as pt-BR currency in the Action.

nodes.label: GET /cliente/detalhe.do?id=
nodes.explanation: Mapping in struts-config.xml: the URL /cliente/detalhe.do triggers DetalheClienteAction with the request-scoped form clienteForm. The customer id arrives as a URL parameter and Struts populates it into the form.

nodes.label: DetalheClienteAction.execute
nodes.explanation: Entry point of the screen. Reads the id from the form, asks the service for the name and the balance, formats the balance as currency and puts it in the request for the JSP. It is the only Action involved for this field.
nodes.migration: Becomes the REST controller. All data assembly here should move to the service; formatting moves to the frontend.

nodes.label: ClienteService.saldoDisponivel
nodes.explanation: Computes the available balance. Fetches balance and blocked amount in a single query and, depending on the person type, decides whether to subtract the blocked amount.
nodes.migration: Core business rule: keep it in the new backend with tests for both PF and PJ.

nodes.label: ClienteDAO.saldoEBloqueado
nodes.explanation: Runs the SELECT on CONTA filtered by customer id and returns an array of two BigDecimal: [0]=SALDO, [1]=BLOQUEADO.
attention: Calls rs.next() and ignores the result: if there is no account, getBigDecimal throws.
Assumes a single account per customer.
nodes.migration: Equivalent repository/query; handle 'customer without account' explicitly (404 or zero balance, decide with the business).

nodes.label: SELECT SALDO, BLOQUEADO FROM CONTA
nodes.explanation: Static SQL in a constant (SQL_SALDO). Uses a PreparedStatement with a bound parameter, so there is no SQL injection risk here.

nodes.label: CONTA.SALDO
nodes.explanation: Column with the account's ledger balance. Read via rs.getBigDecimal("SALDO") and becomes s[0] in the service.

nodes.label: CONTA.BLOQUEADO
nodes.explanation: Amount blocked on the account (e.g. court order, uncleared check). Only used for individuals (PF).

nodes.label: ClienteDAO.isPJ
nodes.explanation: Decides whether the customer is a company (PJ) by looking only at the id length: 14 characters = CNPJ. Does not query the database, despite living in the DAO.
attention: Fragile: a masked id ('12.345.678/0001-90') has 18 characters and would be treated as PF.
Domain rule hidden in the data layer.
nodes.migration: Use an explicit person-type column if one exists; otherwise isolate the rule in a tested domain function.

nodes.label: balance - blocked (PF)
nodes.explanation: For individuals (PF), the displayed balance is the balance minus the blocked amount.

nodes.label: format as pt-BR currency
nodes.explanation: Converts the BigDecimal into Brazilian currency text (e.g. 1234.5 → "R$ 1.234,50"). From here on the value is no longer a number.
attention: Hardcoded new Locale("pt","BR"): ignores the user's language.
nodes.migration: Remove from the backend. The endpoint returns a number; the frontend formats it.

nodes.label: request.saldoFormatado
nodes.explanation: Puts the formatted text in the request under the name 'saldoFormatado'. That is the name the JSP looks up.

nodes.label: Saldo field (detalhe.jsp)
nodes.explanation: The JSP prints the saldoFormatado attribute with <bean:write>, with no further transformation.

edges.label: rs.getBigDecimal("SALDO") → s[0]
edges.explanation: The SALDO column becomes position 0 of the array returned by the DAO.

edges.label: !isPJ(id)
edges.explanation: When the customer is NOT a company, the service subtracts the blocked amount.

edges.label: isPJ(id): s[0] without deduction
edges.explanation: When it is a company, the service returns s[0] directly, no deduction.

rules.text: Company (PJ): displayed balance = SALDO, blocked amount is not subtracted
PJ is detected by the id length (14 chars = CNPJ), not by a database column
Value displayed as Brazilian currency (R$, comma as decimal separator)

attention.text: rs.next() result is ignored: a customer without an account throws an error instead of showing zero
Formatting happens on the server; the page receives ready-made text, not a number
isPJ lives in the DAO but never touches the database: a domain rule in the wrong layer

migration: Suggested endpoint: GET /customers/{id}/balance → { balance: number, blocked: number, available: number, personType: 'PF'|'PJ' }
Return the raw number and format it on the frontend (Intl.NumberFormat('pt-BR', {style:'currency', currency:'BRL'}))

migration.text: Move the PF/PJ rule into the backend domain and cover both cases with tests
